description_full: The Hackett Group, Inc. operates as an intellectual property platform-based generative artificial intelligence strategic consulting and executive advisory digital transformation in the United States, Europe, and internationally. The company offers Hackett AI XPLR, an enterprise-wide Gen AI assessment, ideation and solution design platform; XT, a Gen AIenabled business transformation acceleration platform; AIXelerator, a platform designed to support enterprise application implementation and modernization engagements; Ask Hackett and Hackett Connect, a Gen AIassisted knowledge and insight capability that enables Hackett associates to support delivery of executive advisory and applied intelligence programs; Quantum Leap, a software-as-a-service platform, and Digital Transformation Platform, a platform that translate benchmark insight into actionable execution steps; and ZBrain, a Gen AI engineering and agentic workflow build capability. It also provides Gen AIenabled delivery platforms including, supply chain and operation, finance, human resources, information technology, procurement, corporate services, as well as selected enterprise application implementation services, including Oracle, SAP, OneStream, and eProcurement applications. In addition, the company offers oracle solutions that help clients to choose and deploy oracle applications that meet needs and objectives; SAP solutions, including planning, architecture, and vendor evaluation and selection through implementation, customization, testing, and integration; post-implementation support, change and exception management, process transparency, system documentation, and end-user training; off-shore application development, and application maintenance and support services; and sells SAP suite of applications. The company was formerly known as Answerthink, Inc. and changed its name to The Hackett Group, Inc. in 2008. The Hackett Group, Inc. was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Miami, Florida.

financial_summary: The Hackett Group, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $330M market cap on $306M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 39% against a 8% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 29%.

The business throws off $32M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 24.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 8% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.33x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-5.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 35% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 22% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 36% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 53% and a beta of 0.91, it moves roughly with the market.
About $2.2M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash, 28% in the 2022 bear market and 73% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 64% below its DCF fair value of $36.54, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 54%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $24.92 to $54.70 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 19.3 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 9.5 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 10.2 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 34% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 9.8% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $17.33 on average, 30% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 39% clears the cost of capital of 8.1% by 30pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.46).
It runs a 29% gross margin and converts 11% of revenue into free cash flow, or 7% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 3.11x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.0x equity multiplier).
It spends 3.6% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.0x net debt to EBITDA ($18.2M of cash against $75.8M of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 13.7x.
Goodwill makes up 44% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.3% over 3 years and 1.6% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Capex runs 1.5x depreciation (2.6% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Analysts expect 9.1% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 12.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 84%.
It returns 24.8% a year to shareholders (20.9% in buybacks and 3.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 13 consecutive years, raising it 2.9% a year over the last five.
people: With about 1,503 employees, each generates about $203K of revenue, 0.5x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 2.2% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $22K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.3M (6x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
